{"parentUuid":"8a7a41f6-16f0-4372-a987-1658ef7a2a17","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_015dxB7pfz5ppeXZe3XrWCoB","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_012SuZAcD3SpfmAYr5iyCena","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\try-n-approaches\\SKILL.md","content":"---\nname: try-n-approaches\ndescription: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\nallowed-tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write]\n---\n\n# Skill: try-n-approaches\n\n## Purpose\n\nPer D-003 § 5.5c.3 + UP-06 §3 (verbatim \"kết hợp với idea của karpathy autoresearch\") + S12 DSPy dogfood (`learning-data/dogfood/dspy.md`): when stockforge surfaces a question of the form \"what should we do next about signal X?\", DO NOT pick the first plausible approach. Instead generate ≥3 distinct approach families, evaluate via a deterministic metric, pick the cheapest competent one, and commit a falsifiable measurement plan.\n\nThe skill's deliverable is the FRAMING ARTIFACT (one markdown file at `learning-data/loop/<TS>-experiment-frame.md`). Execution of the picked approach happens AFTER framing — by the next session, by a dispatched subagent, or by a deterministic hook. Framing IS the work this skill does.\n\nConsumer of S12 dogfood pattern: per L-S12-1, EVERY framing this skill emits MUST cite a deterministic metric function (formula + baseline + target + falsification clause). No metric → describe the experiment, do NOT claim improvement.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Drift signal fires repeatedly + agent must decide whether to deepen the fix or pivot\n- Dogfood insight surfaces a gap (e.g., S12 DSPy → metric-function gap in stockforge loop)\n- Sync-grilling hook surfaces user-vs-current divergence + multiple resolution paths exist\n- Capability-map shows ≥3 limit observations clustering on one task class — pick remediation\n- Open question in current-execution.md \"Current Work Items\" tagged as exploratory\n\n## When NOT to Use\n\n- Task is single-path obvious (just do it; framing is overhead)\n- Task is purely deterministic (script it; no metric needed)\n- Already mid-execution and framing post-hoc would be a postmortem\n- Budget-pressured session — framing is upstream work, skip if windowed for IMPL\n\n## Inputs\n\n| Arg | Required | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|\n| `question` | yes | The open question in 1-2 sentences. Quote verbatim from triggering signal. |\n| `--inputs` | yes | Comma-separated paths to source artifacts (drift log / dogfood insight / categories file). Each becomes a `provenance` row. |\n| `--n-approaches` | no | Cap on approaches generated. Default `3` (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON). Range [3,5]. |\n| `--metric-function` | yes | Path or inline definition of the deterministic metric. Failing this argument = skill REFUSES per L-S12-1. |\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Parse question** — quote it verbatim. Don't paraphrase yet — paraphrase loses signal in DSPy-pattern terms.\n2. **Read inputs** — every `--inputs` path becomes a row in the provenance table with as_of date. Cite source-of-truth not memory.\n3. **Identify prior state** — what does the corpus / signal look like RIGHT NOW? Cite numbers from index/categories or last metric run, not from impression.\n4. **Generate ≥3 approaches** in three families:\n   - **DEEPEN** — instrument the rung that's currently null/under-measured; smallest unit of work that resolves the most caveats\n   - **BROADEN** — grow the corpus / sample / coverage; bigger denominator\n   - **ABANDON** — drop the bucket / signal / class; admit it's structurally absent\n   - For each: action / cost (~tokens, sessions) / why-this / falsification path\n5. **Pick one per cheap-first doctrine** (per `decompose-work` heuristic + capability-map L-1/L-2): smallest unit of work that resolves the most caveats AND has a deterministic falsification path. Document why the rejected options are rejected (anti-AP-1 echo chamber).\n6. **Attach metric function** (BLOCKING per L-S12-1) — must be deterministic (Python or bash, no LLM judgment) + formula + baseline value with `n_samples` + as_of + target + falsification clause + calibration metadata.\n7. **Adversarial bear case** — list ≥3 distinct risks in the picked direction. Apply charter P3 (\"adversarial by design\") at framing time, not at outcome time.\n8. **State what the experiment is NOT** — bound the claim. Per S12 framing pattern: NOT a thesis, NOT a runtime change, NOT optimization, NOT a charter amendment.\n9. **Write provenance log** — every cited fact maps to source URL/path + as_of + commit-or-snapshot.\n10. **Outcome stub** — frontmatter has `outcome: pending`; later filled at next loop iteration with `decision_at_outcome_review: deepen-confirmed | broaden | abandon`.\n11. **Write artifact** — `Write agent-workspace/learning-data/loop/<TS>-experiment-frame.md` per `references/output-template.md`.\n\n## Validation Pre-Conditions\n\n- `--metric-function` is non-empty (else REFUSE — per L-S12-1)\n- ≥3 approaches present in DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families\n- Picked direction has a falsification clause (charter P9 + P3)\n- ≥3 distinct adversarial risks listed (charter P3)\n- Provenance table covers ALL cited facts (charter P1 evidence-grounding)\n- Frontmatter `metric_function:` field MATCHES the function in body §Measurement plan\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- **Skipping the metric function** — without it, \"self-learning\" is vibes; per L-S12-1 the skill REFUSES.\n- **Single-approach framing** — if you can only think of one approach, that's a 1-step plan, not a Karpathy loop. Drop the skill; just do the step.\n- **Picking DEEPEN by default** — sometimes BROADEN is the right call (corpus too small to detect rare events) or ABANDON is right (signal genuinely absent). Cheap-first ordering MUST consider all three.\n- **LLM-generated metric** — metric must be code (Python/bash); LLM proposing a \"feel\" metric violates I-S1 (no LLM math).\n- **Outcome stub left blank** — frontmatter must have `outcome: pending` so the next loop iteration knows to revisit.\n- **Confusing \"framing\" with \"execution\"** — this skill writes the plan; the plan is executed elsewhere. Don't conflate.\n- **Re-doing framing on every signal fire** — once a frame is committed, the next loop iteration UPDATES the existing frame (writes outcome) before generating a new one. Otherwise loop history rots.\n\n## Smoke Test (S13 first run)\n\nSample question: *\"Given the corpus state at S12 close (60 events / 0 failure_mode populated / 5 promotion-candidate components) and the DSPy dogfood insight, what is the next experiment that maximizes information gain per token spent?\"*\n\nExpected framing shape (target):\n- DEEPEN → wire failure_mode in component-telemetry.sh + author metric script (~100K, 1 session)\n- BROADEN → wait 3-4 sessions for 200-event corpus, re-run L-1 (~36K)\n- ABANDON → drop drift/retry/mistake-type buckets, simplify L-1 (~20K, 1 session)\n- Picked: DEEPEN (3 independent signals converge; BROADEN requires DEEPEN first; ABANDON confuses uninstrumented with absent)\n- Metric function: `failure_mode_populated_rate = count(events.failure_mode != null) / count(events)` (baseline 0/60=0%, target ≥8.3%)\n\nThis was the actual S12 framing artifact (`learning-data/loop/20260429T131608Z-experiment-frame.md`); the skill formalizes that pattern for future loops.\n\nPass criteria: skill produces a frame matching template; metric function field non-empty + cited in body; ≥3 approaches with cost-and-falsification; ≥3 bear-points; outcome=pending.\n\n## Output Schema (frontmatter)\n\n```yaml\n---\nexperiment_id: loop-frame-<TS>\ncreated_at: <ISO-8601>\nsession: S<N> (Track <T>)\nframing_decision: DEEPEN | BROADEN | ABANDON\ninputs:\n  - <path-1>\n  - <path-2>\nas_of: <YYYY-MM-DD>\nmetric_function: <path-or-inline-name>     # BLOCKING per L-S12-1\noutcome: pending                           # filled at next iteration\n---\n```\n\nBody sections (mandatory order): Question / Prior state / Three options / Picked direction / Measurement plan / Risks / What this is NOT / Provenance / Outcome.\n\n## See Also\n\n- `agent-workspace/learning-data/dogfood/dspy.md` — pattern source (deterministic metric function as bridge)\n- `agent-workspace/learning-data/loop/20260429T131608Z-experiment-frame.md` — first instance + template reference\n- `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md § L-S12-1` — metric_function-required rule (BINDING)\n- `.claude/skills/decompose-work/SKILL.md` — sibling 5.5c.1; deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach\n- `.claude/skills/promote-rule/SKILL.md` — sibling 5.5c.6; consumes loop outcomes for cluster promotion\n- `agent-workspace/memory/capability-map.md` — strength/limit grounding for approach scoring\n- `scripts/hooks/metric-failure-mode-rate.sh` — first deterministic metric (S13 first instance)\n- D-003 § 5.5c.3 + UP-06 §3 — strategic rationale\n- charter principles 1 (evidence) + 3 (adversarial) + 8 (calibration) + 9 (no LLM math)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3246,"cache_read_input_tokens":169763,"output_tokens":4583,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3246,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":4583,"cache_read_input_tokens":169763,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3246,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3246},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYAcTMgLwTiY7NjgHmHL","type":"assistant","uuid":"b2433053-2b1d-438c-909a-0787c97b2f76","timestamp":"2026-04-29T13:48:07.687Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"09d3d5a4-dfd0-4201-ab96-9e5ba7609718","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

Per S12 framing pattern: NOT a thesis, NOT a runtime change, NOT optimization, NOT a charter amendment.\n9. **Write provenance log** — every cited fact maps to source URL/path + as_of + commit-or-snapshot.\n10. **Outcome stub** — frontmatter has `outcome: pending`; later filled at next loop iteration with `decision_at_outcome_review: deepen-confirmed | broaden | abandon`.\n11. **Write artifact** — `Write agent-workspace/learning-data/loop/<TS>-experiment-frame.md` per `references/output-template.md`.\n\n## Validation Pre-Conditions\n\n- `--metric-function` is non-empty (else REFUSE — per L-S12-1)\n- ≥3 approaches present in DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families\n- Picked direction has a falsification clause (charter P9 + P3)\n- ≥3 distinct adversarial risks listed (charter P3)\n- Provenance table covers ALL cited facts (charter P1 evidence-grounding)\n- Frontmatter `metric_function:` field MATCHES the function in body §Measurement plan\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- **Skipping the metric function** — without it, \"self-learning\" is vibes; per L-S12-1 the skill REFUSES.\n- **Single-approach framing** — if you can only think of one approach, that's a 1-step plan, not a Karpathy loop. Drop the skill; just do the step.\n- **Picking DEEPEN by default** — sometimes BROADEN is the right call (corpus too small to detect rare events) or ABANDON is right (signal genuinely absent). Cheap-first ordering MUST consider all three.\n- **LLM-generated metric** — metric must be code (Python/bash); LLM proposing a \"feel\" metric violates I-S1 (no LLM math).\n- **Outcome stub left blank** — frontmatter must have `outcome: pending` so the next loop iteration knows to revisit.\n- **Confusing \"framing\" with \"execution\"** — this skill writes the plan; the plan is executed elsewhere. Don't conflate.\n- **Re-doing framing on every signal fire** — once a frame is committed, the next loop iteration UPDATES the existing frame (writes outcome) before generating a new one. Otherwise loop history rots.\n\n## Smoke Test (S13 first run)\n\nSample question: *\"Given the corpus state at S12 close (60 events / 0 failure_mode populated / 5 promotion-candidate components) and the DSPy dogfood insight, what is the next experiment that maximizes information gain per token spent?\"*\n\nExpected framing shape (target):\n- DEEPEN → wire failure_mode in component-telemetry.sh + author metric script (~100K, 1 session)\n- BROADEN → wait 3-4 sessions for 200-event corpus, re-run L-1 (~36K)\n- ABANDON → drop drift/retry/mistake-type buckets, simplify L-1 (~20K, 1 session)\n- Picked: DEEPEN (3 independent signals converge; BROADEN requires DEEPEN first; ABANDON confuses uninstrumented with absent)\n- Metric function: `failure_mode_populated_rate = count(events.failure_mode != null) / count(events)` (baseline 0/60=0%, target ≥8.3%)\n\nThis was the actual S12 framing artifact (`learning-data/loop/20260429T131608Z-experiment-frame.md`); the skill formalizes that pattern for future loops.\n\nPass criteria: skill produces a frame matching template; metric function field non-empty + cited in body; ≥3 approaches with cost-and-falsification; ≥3 bear-points; outcome=pending.\n\n## Output Schema (frontmatter)\n\n```yaml\n---\nexperiment_id: loop-frame-<TS>\ncreated_at: <ISO-8601>\nsession: S<N> (Track <T>)\nframing_decision: DEEPEN | BROADEN | ABANDON\ninputs:\n  - <path-1>\n  - <path-2>\nas_of: <YYYY-MM-DD>\nmetric_function: <path-or-inline-name>     # BLOCKING per L-S12-1\noutcome: pending                           # filled at next iteration\n---\n```\n\nBody sections (mandatory order): Question / Prior state / Three options / Picked direction / Measurement plan / Risks / What this is NOT / Provenance / Outcome.\n\n## See Also\n\n- `agent-workspace/learning-data/dogfood/dspy.md` — pattern source (deterministic metric function as bridge)\n- `agent-workspace/learning-data/loop/20260429T131608Z-experiment-frame.md` — first instance + template reference\n- `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md § L-S12-1` — metric_function-required rule (BINDING)\n- `.claude/skills/decompose-work/SKILL.md` — sibling 5.5c.1; deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach\n- `.claude/skills/promote-rule/SKILL.md` — sibling 5.5c.6; consumes loop outcomes for cluster promotion\n- `agent-workspace/memory/capability-map.md` — strength/limit grounding for approach scoring\n- `scripts/hooks/metric-failure-mode-rate.sh` — first deterministic metric (S13 first instance)\n- D-003 § 5.5c.3 + UP-06 §3 — strategic rationale\n- charter principles 1 (evidence) + 3 (adversarial) + 8 (calibration) + 9 (no LLM math)\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b2433053-2b1d-438c-909a-0787c97b2f76","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"09d3d5a4-dfd0-4201-ab96-9e5ba7609718","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"ef6c7d72-278f-4a78-88ba-609fa880ee8b","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. {"parentUuid":"10919e08-e1d2-4344-853a-81e7f11a7d50","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01PN35s2XFfUiZMoSc7PCdnX","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01U7GDpZPojKvXrV1FJG8V95","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\memory\\self-awareness\\jsonl-schema.md","content":"---\nschema_version: 2\ncreated_at: 2026-04-29 (S13 — Track 5.5c.5)\nupdated_at: 2026-04-29\ndescription: |\n  JSONL telemetry schema for stockforge harness self-awareness loop. Two streams:\n  (1) component-telemetry.jsonl — flat per-tool event log, rotated at 10 MB.\n  (2) learning-data/events/<UTC-date>.ndjson — write-heavy ETL stream for L-1 classifier.\n  This document is the source-of-truth for both. Schema extension drives loop closure\n  (task_id + approach_id + metric let outcomes attribute back to the framing artifact).\nsource_decision: agent-workspace/memory/decisions/003-up06-track-5.5-sync-layer-selfcap.md § 5.5c.5\nrelated_artifacts:\n  - scripts/hooks/component-telemetry.sh    # producer\n  - scripts/hooks/learning-index-rebuild.sh # consumer (RAG index path)\n  - scripts/hooks/metric-failure-mode-rate.sh # consumer (metric path)\n  - .claude/skills/try-n-approaches/SKILL.md  # producer of task_id/approach_id (Phase 1+)\n  - agent-workspace/learning-data/loop/      # outcome attribution target\n---\n\n# JSONL Telemetry Schema\n\n> Schema for both stockforge telemetry streams. Versioned. Backward-compatible by default\n> (new fields are optional + default null); breaking changes bump `schema_version`.\n\n## Stream A: component-telemetry.jsonl (flat event log)\n\nPath: `agent-workspace/memory/component-telemetry.jsonl` (rotated to `.1`..`.5` at 10 MB).\nProducer: `scripts/hooks/component-telemetry.sh` (PostToolUse / SubagentStop / SessionStart hook).\nConsumer: drift signals + ad-hoc grep.\n\n### Fields (S13 close)\n\n| Field | Type | Status | Source | Notes |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `ts` | string (ISO-8601 UTC, ms) | shipped S8 | `date -u +%FT%T.%3NZ` | event timestamp |\n| `component_type` | string | shipped S8 | classify_component() | one of: hook / agent / skill / command |\n| `component_name` | string | shipped S8 | classify_component() | tool name, agent type, or skill name |\n| `trigger` | string | shipped S8 | classify_component() | hook_event / agent_dispatch / keyword_match / explicit_invoke |\n| `outcome` | string | shipped S8 | OUTCOME var | ok / error / timeout / reject / no_op |\n| `tokens_real` | int | shipped S8 | compute_tokens_real() | delta from `.transcript-tokens` |\n| `duration_ms` | int | shipped S8 | compute_duration_ms() | wall-clock from prior event |\n| `session_id` | string \\| null | shipped S8 | payload.session_id | Claude Code session UUID |\n| `task_id` | string \\| null | **always null today (S13)** | reserved | wires from try-n-approaches frame at Phase 1+ |\n| `failure_mode` | string \\| null | **shipped S13** | correlate_failure_mode() + outcome fallback | A/B/C/D/H/P/T (see § Failure mode codes) |\n\n### Phase 1+ extensions (S14+)\n\n| Field | Type | Status | Notes |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `approach_id` | string \\| null | designed (5.5c.5) | links event to N-approach branch from try-n-approaches frame |\n| `metric` | string \\| null | designed (5.5c.5) | name of deterministic metric function evaluating this event (per L-S12-1) |\n\n## Stream B: learning-data/events/<UTC-date>.ndjson (ETL store)\n\nPath: `agent-workspace/learning-data/events/YYYY-MM-DD.ndjson` (boundary: gitignored + runtime read-deny per D9).\nProducer: `scripts/hooks/component-telemetry.sh` (same hook; emit_learning_event() wraps the payload).\nConsumer: L-1 classifier dispatch (background sonnet); metric scripts; `learning-index-rebuild.sh`.\n\n### Wrapper schema (S13 close)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"ts\": \"<ISO-8601 UTC ms>\",\n  \"source\": \"component-telemetry.sh\",\n  \"event_type\": \"harness-component-event\",\n  \"payload\": { /* same fields as Stream A, minus the wrapper */ },\n  \"as_of\": \"<YYYY-MM-DD>\"\n}\n```\n\n`as_of` is per I-S2 (point-in-time integrity) — bucket date for which the event was emitted (UTC).\n\n### Phase 1+ extensions for Stream B\n\nSame as Stream A: `approach_id`, `metric` populate inside `payload`.\n\n## Failure mode codes (S13 wire-in)\n\n| Code | Meaning | Source | S13 status |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `A` | agent narration drift (LLM ended turn without producing artifact) | reserved (LLM-side detector) | NOT WIRED |\n| `B` | api / tool error | outcome=error fallback | wired |\n| `C` | premature wind-down (mode-C guard fired) | `.autonomous-premature-windown-alert.log` correlate | wired |\n| `D` | drift signal threshold exceeded | reserved (constant-fire today; gated until D-thresholds tuned) | NOT WIRED |\n| `H` | permission deny (PAYLOAD_DECISION=\"deny\") | dispatch-site override | wired |\n| `P` | cliff auto-reboot fire | `.session-hooks.log` correlate within current minute | wired |\n| `T` | tool timeout | outcome=timeout fallback | wired |\n| `null` | no failure detected | default | wired |\n\nOrdering in dispatch: correlate first (A/C/D/P) → outcome fallback (B/T) → deny override (H).\nH takes precedence because the deny information is authoritative (came directly from the harness).\n\n## Consumer contract\n\n- Stream A (component-telemetry.jsonl): drift signal scripts + ad-hoc grep. NEVER loaded into LLM context.\n- Stream B (learning-data/events/): write-only-during-runtime; read by RAG path (`index/`) + classifier dispatch + metric scripts. NEVER loaded into LLM context directly (D9 enforces).\n- Schema changes: any new field is OPTIONAL + defaults `null`. Breaking changes bump `schema_version`. Never silent-rename a field — append + deprecate.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- Loading raw `events/*.ndjson` into runtime context. Always go via `index/` (D9 violation).\n- Renaming a field without bump. Loops break silently because consumers grep field names.\n- Synthesizing metrics inside the LLM. Per I-S1: metric values come from code; LLM only interprets.\n- Adding a Phase 1+ field (e.g., `approach_id`) and treating its null today as bug. It's by design until try-n-approaches wires the producer side.\n\n## Version history\n\n- `v1` (S8): shipped flat 9-field schema (no failure_mode, no learning-data wrapper)\n- `v2` (S13): added `failure_mode` (wired); designed `approach_id` + `metric` (Phase 1+); learning-data wrapper formalized\n\n## See also\n\n- D-003 § 5.5c.5 — strategic rationale (UP-06 §3)\n- agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md § L-S12-1 — metric_function-required rule\n- agent-workspace/learning-data/README.md — boundary contract\n- scripts/hooks/component-telemetry.sh — producer (canonical implementation)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4915,"cache_read_input_tokens":177718,"output_tokens":3930,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4915,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":3930,"cache_read_input_tokens":177718,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4915,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4915},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYAisDHt3PpCDpg2UE2e","type":"assistant","uuid":"1ca95fea-82a4-4dc7-8192-3575f3f84316","timestamp":"2026-04-29T13:49:22.685Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"09d3d5a4-dfd0-4201-ab96-9e5ba7609718","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"29d3c96a-097b-4e81-8495-77d0ba4d91d9","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01VB6sLEf6Rbm54zcdHxHbT1","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01WNs51ARZ4X72yRS1nT81SH","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\memory\\self-awareness\\otel-design.md","content":"---\nartifact_id: otel-design-s13\ncreated_at: 2026-04-29 (S13 — Track 5.5c.4)\nstatus: DESIGN-ONLY (Phase 0); collector docker deferred to Phase 1+ entry\ndescription: |\n  Design-only artifact for the OTEL stack referenced in D-003 § 5.5c.4. Implementation deferred\n  per Phase 0 portability rule (L-S11-1: bash + node + POSIX only at hook level; Docker is Phase 1+).\n  This document captures the architecture so Phase 1+ implementation has a written target.\nsource_decision: agent-workspace/memory/decisions/003-up06-track-5.5-sync-layer-selfcap.md § 5.5c.4\ndeferral_basis:\n  - \"L-S11-1 (Phase 0 portability — bash + node + POSIX only at hook level; no docker)\"\n  - \"D-003 risk register: 'If 5.5c overshoots, descope c.4 OTEL to design-only + defer collector docker to Track 9'\"\nrelated_artifacts:\n  - agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/jsonl-schema.md  # current telemetry source-of-truth\n  - scripts/hooks/component-telemetry.sh                    # current emitter (JSONL)\n  - agent-workspace/memory/decisions/003-up06-track-5.5-sync-layer-selfcap.md\n---\n\n# OTEL Stack Design — Phase 1+ Activation Target\n\n> Stockforge currently uses bash + NDJSON for self-awareness telemetry. This document specifies\n> the OTEL collector + emitter stack that will replace the per-tool telemetry path once Phase 1+\n> Docker deployment exists. Until then: design-only; no docker-compose runs at Phase 0.\n\n## Why OTEL eventually (rationale from D-003)\n\nJSONL alone suffices for current scale (~100-300 events/session, single dev machine). OTEL adds:\n- **Standard tooling**: Jaeger / Tempo / Honeycomb consumers exist; team or peer-share trivially.\n- **Distributed correlation**: when Phase 2+ adds multi-service pipelines (data ingest + classifier + dashboard), span trees beat flat NDJSON for debugging cross-service flows.\n- **Sampling control**: OTEL collector can do head/tail sampling; JSONL is \"collect everything or nothing\".\n- **Vendor-neutral exporters**: can swap Jaeger → Tempo → cloud without rewriting emitters.\n\nCost: ~200K one-time setup (per D-003 plan estimate). Phase 0 deferral acceptable.\n\n## Phase 0 (current) — bash + NDJSON only\n\nProducer: `scripts/hooks/component-telemetry.sh` (PostToolUse / SubagentStop / SessionStart).\nOutput: `learning-data/events/<date>.ndjson` (per Stream B in jsonl-schema.md).\nConsumers: `learning-index-rebuild.sh` (RAG index), `metric-failure-mode-rate.sh` (deterministic metrics).\nNo collector, no spans, no docker. **This is sufficient for stockforge Phase 0 single-dev scale.**\n\n## Phase 1+ activation plan\n\nWhen Docker deployment lands (Phase 1 — `docker-compose.yml` already designed in `docker-compose.yml` at repo root for Postgres + Redis):\n\n### Service: otel-collector (new, ~50 LOC docker-compose section)\n\n```yaml\notel-collector:\n  image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.96.0  # pin version; update on release schedule\n  command: [\"--config=/etc/otel/config.yaml\"]\n  volumes:\n    - ./docker/otel-stack/config.yaml:/etc/otel/config.yaml:ro\n    - otel-data:/var/lib/otel  # local file exporter for Phase 1; swap for Jaeger/Tempo later\n  ports:\n    - \"4317:4317\"  # OTLP gRPC\n    - \"4318:4318\"  # OTLP HTTP\n  restart: unless-stopped\n```\n\n### Receiver / processor / exporter pipeline (`docker/otel-stack/config.yaml`)\n\n```yaml\nreceivers:\n  otlp:\n    protocols: { grpc: {}, http: {} }\nprocessors:\n  batch: {}              # 5s batch window — keep collector overhead bounded\n  resource:\n    attributes:\n      - key: service.name\n        value: stockforge\n        action: insert\nexporters:\n  file:\n    path: /var/lib/otel/spans.jsonl   # Phase 1 default; swap for jaeger/tempo at Phase 2+\nservice:\n  pipelines:\n    traces:\n      receivers: [otlp]\n      processors: [batch, resource]\n      exporters: [file]\n```\n\n### Python emitter: `packages/observability/otel_emitter.py`\n\nPhase 1+ emitter (NOT TO BE WRITTEN AT PHASE 0). Wraps `opentelemetry-api` + `opentelemetry-sdk`.\nUsed from Python services (data ingest, classifier, dashboard) — NOT from bash hooks (hooks stay\non bash + NDJSON; bridge written by collector if hooks ever need OTEL output).\n\n### Bash hook bridge (Phase 1+ optional)\n\n`component-telemetry.sh` could OPTIONALLY POST to `localhost:4318/v1/traces` if collector reachable.\nBridge keeps NDJSON as authoritative + emits parallel OTEL span. Implementation: ~20 LOC bash via curl + node-eval JSON construction. Skipped at Phase 0 (curl isn't on L-S11-1 whitelist).\n\n## Mapping JSONL → OTEL spans (when wired)\n\nEach NDJSON event becomes 1 OTEL span:\n\n| NDJSON field | OTEL span field |\n|---|---|\n| `ts` | span start_time |\n| `duration_ms` | end_time - start_time |\n| `component_type`, `component_name` | span name (`<type>:<name>`) |\n| `trigger` | span attribute `harness.trigger` |\n| `outcome` | span status (ok/error/etc) |\n| `tokens_real` | span attribute `harness.tokens_real` |\n| `failure_mode` | span attribute `harness.failure_mode` (or null tag) |\n| `session_id` | span attribute `harness.session_id` (cross-session trace correlation) |\n| `task_id`, `approach_id` (Phase 1+) | trace_id linking back to try-n-approaches frame |\n| `metric` (Phase 1+) | span event with metric_name + metric_value |\n\n`approach_id` becomes the trace correlation key — all events emitted while approach X is \"active\" share trace_id, so a span tree shows the full DEEPEN-or-BROADEN execution arc.\n\n## Open IMPL-tier decisions (deferred to Phase 1+)\n\n- **Sampling rate**: head-sample 100% at small scale (low cost) vs tail-sample at higher volume. Default Phase 1: head 100%.\n- **Exporter target**: file (Phase 1) vs Jaeger UI (Phase 2 if peer-share happens) vs Tempo (Phase 3+ if multi-tenant).\n- **Bash bridge**: OPT-IN or always-on? Default OPT-IN — collector reachable check + env flag.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Wiring OTEL emitter at Phase 0**: docker dependency violates L-S11-1 portability. Defer.\n- **Skipping JSONL after OTEL lands**: NDJSON remains authoritative even at Phase 1+. OTEL is a parallel emit, not a replacement. NDJSON is the audit-trail-of-record per D-005 § 5.5d ETL doctrine.\n- **LLM-generated span attributes**: same as I-S1 — values come from code; LLM never invents numeric attributes.\n- **Mixing harness telemetry with stock-domain telemetry in same trace**: harness traces stay in service.name=stockforge-harness; stock-domain spans (Phase 2+) go to service.name=stockforge-pipeline. Separation is identity-tier (charter principle 1).\n\n## See also\n\n- D-003 § 5.5c.4 (deliverable spec)\n- D-003 § Risk register (descope authorization)\n- agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md § L-S11-1 (Phase 0 portability rule)\n- agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/jsonl-schema.md (sibling — current telemetry source-of-truth)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3987,"cache_read_input_tokens":182633,"output_tokens":3542,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3987,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":3542,"cache_read_input_tokens":182633,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3987,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3987},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYAobUPN71pqooKaeCb6","type":"assistant","uuid":"98abc7f5-c2eb-4d3c-9084-737d2b429138","timestamp":"2026-04-29T13:50:15.315Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"09d3d5a4-dfd0-4201-ab96-9e5ba7609718","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"58d7eec4-63be-4fa0-aaef-ad29c839357d","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"7c82c20a-fb0a-4e22-bfc0-81261591498c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01A9vjiJkBzV3cQa1nPnSJQ4","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\learning-data\\loop\\20260429T131608Z-experiment-frame.md has been updated successfully."}]},"uuid":"1e2901c3-ab7f-4496-a61d-c9b422efaedb","timestamp":"2026-04-29T13:53:04.700Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\learning-data\\loop\\20260429T131608Z-experiment-frame.md","oldString":"metric_function: not-yet-authored  # this experiment IS the prerequisite to authoring one","newString":"metric_function: scripts/hooks/metric-failure-mode-rate.sh  # authored S13 (Track 5.5c.3 wire-in); first-pass result documented in agent-workspace/learning-data/index/metrics-<TS>.json","originalFile":"---\nexperiment_id: loop-frame-20260429T131608Z\ncreated_at: 2026-04-29T13:16:08Z\nsession: S12 (Track 5.5d.3)\nframing_decision: DEEPEN\ninputs:\n  - agent-workspace/learning-data/index/categories-20260429T123210Z.md  # S11 L-1 first classification (60 events; 0/0/0/49/11 distribution)\n  - agent-workspace/learning-data/dogfood/dspy.md                       # S12 DSPy pattern insight (metric-function gap)\n  - agent-workspace/learning-data/dogfood/agent-pick-1-research-report-20260429T131201Z.md  # S12 research-scanner survey\nas_of: 2026-04-29\nmetric_function: not-yet-authored  # this experiment IS the prerequisite to authoring one\n---\n\n# Karpathy Outer-Loop Frame — Experiment #1\n\n> First Karpathy autoresearch framing for stockforge harness self-learning. Per D-005 § 5.5d.3\n> Phase 7 + UP-08 verbatim \"kết hợp với idea của karpathy autoresearch\". Pattern from\n> `.claude/skills/decompose-work/SKILL.md` (try-n-approaches not yet shipped — S13).\n\n## Question\n\nGiven the corpus state at S12 close (60 events / all-ok / no failure_mode populated / 5 promotion-candidate components) and the DSPy dogfood insight (deterministic metric function is the missing bridge), what is the next experiment that maximizes information gain per token spent?\n\n## Prior state — what S11 + S12 produced\n\n**S11 (Track 5.5d.2)**: First L-1 classification dispatch. 60 events. Distribution `0/0/0/49/11` (drift / retry / mistake-type / promotion-candidate / uncategorized). Six adversarial caveats documented; two are load-bearing for this framing:\n\n- Caveat #1: drift bucket may be structurally undercount — `component-telemetry.sh` may not emit on denied tool calls.\n- Caveat #2: `failure_mode` field is null on 60/60 events — possibly uninstrumented, not falsified.\n\n**S12 (Track 5.5d.3)**: Agent-pick-1 dogfood. DSPy picked. Pattern insight: stockforge has a self-learning loop with no metric function — without a deterministic scalar/categorical comparing run N+1 to run N, no version of the pipeline can be claimed \"better than\" another.\n\n## Three options on the table\n\n### Option A — DEEPEN (instrument the missing rungs)\n\n**Action**: Wire `failure_mode` field population in `component-telemetry.sh` from `correlate_failure_mode()` already drafted in `.autonomous-stop-watchdog.log` reads. Then author **one** deterministic metric function (the `failure_mode population rate` from dogfood/dspy.md § metric candidates) and re-run L-1 on a fresh ≥60-event corpus to compare.\n\n**What it costs**: ~1 hook-edit session (~30-50K). One metric script (~30 LOC bash or python). One re-dispatch of L-1 classifier (~36K, observed cost from S11). Estimated total: 1 session ≤100K. Fits S13/S14 alongside try-n-approaches ship.\n\n**Why this option**: Two highest-confidence caveats from S11 (drift undercount + failure_mode null) both resolve via the same fix path. The DSPy dogfood ALSO points to the same gap (metric function). Three independent signals (S11 caveat #1, caveat #2, DSPy insight) converging on one fix = strong deepen prior.\n\n**What we measure** (explicit, falsifiable):\n- Metric: `failure_mode_populated = count(events where failure_mode != null) / count(events total)`\n- Baseline (S11): 0/60 = 0.0%\n- Target (S12+1): ≥ 5/60 = 8.3% on next 60-event corpus\n- Falsification: if after instrumentation, the rate is still 0% AND no failures occurred = harness too stable to instrument; loop signal exhausted; PIVOT to Option B (broaden corpus to find rare events). If rate ≥ 8.3% = instrumentation works; advance to second metric (drift signal precision).\n\n### Option B — BROADEN (grow the corpus)\n\n**Action**: Increase corpus from 60 events to 200+ before next L-1 dispatch. Currently events accumulate naturally per session (~30-60 events per major session per S11 observation). Wait 3-4 sessions and re-run L-1.\n\n**What it costs**: 0 token cost in new sessions (events emit free); 1 re-dispatch (~36K).\n\n**Why this option might be tempting**: bigger corpus = more statistical power for rare-event detection (the <5% pattern blind-spot from S11 caveat #5).\n\n**Why this option is wrong now**: at 0% failure_mode population, broadening to 200 events still yields 0/200 — adding null data doesn't improve signal. Broaden is the right move AFTER instrumentation fix; before fix, it just delays the same problem.\n\n### Option C — ABANDON (delete the zero-signal buckets)\n\n**Action**: Delete drift / retry / mistake-type categories from L-1 spec; keep only promotion-candidate + uncategorized. Acknowledge harness is too clean to have negative signal worth tracking at Phase 0 scale.\n\n**Why this option might be tempting**: simpler classifier; no instrumentation work needed.\n\n**Why this option is wrong**: it confuses \"field uninstrumented\" with \"signal absent\". S11 caveat #2 explicitly noted: \"`mistake-type` and `drift` buckets are not falsified — they are simply uninstrumented.\" Abandoning a bucket because the field hasn't been wired = closing the loop on negative information that may exist. Charter principle 3 (adversarial by design) prefers asking \"is the absence real\" over \"assume absence is real\".\n\n## Picked direction — DEEPEN (Option A)\n\nRationale: convergence of 3 independent signals on the same fix; Option B requires Option A first; Option C confuses uninstrumented with absent (charter P3 violation).\n\nCheap-first ordering doctrine satisfied: A is the smallest unit of work that resolves the most caveats per token spent.\n\n## Measurement plan (explicit; this is the metric function S13 will codify)\n\n```\nmetric: failure_mode_populated_rate\nformula: count(events where failure_mode IS NOT null) / count(events total)\nimplementation: bash + python3 oneliner in scripts/hooks/learning-index-rebuild.sh\n                (extend existing hook; do NOT add new infra)\nbaseline:    0.0% (S11 corpus, n=60, observed 2026-04-29)\ntarget:      >= 8.3% (S12+1 corpus, n>=60, observed at first L-1 re-dispatch)\nfalsification: if rate < 8.3% AND no failures occurred in the corpus window\n               (deterministically: count(.autonomous-stop-watchdog.log entries) > 0\n                vs count(events with failure_mode != null) — if log shows failures\n                but events show null, instrumentation fix was incomplete)\ncalibration:   record n_samples + lookback_window in result; per charter P8\n```\n\nThis metric is **deterministic** (counts, no LLM judgment), **falsifiable** (specific threshold), **calibration-aware** (records sample size + lookback per L-2), and **cheap** (extends an existing hook; no new dependency). Matches DSPy's metric-function pattern as adapted in dogfood/dspy.md.\n\n## Risks (≥3 distinct, per charter P3 adversarial)\n\n1. **Failure mode classifier drift**: if `correlate_failure_mode()` is buggy (e.g., over-classifies stop-watchdog entries as failures), the rate will jump artificially. Mitigation: smoke-test the function with `LEARNING_INDEX_FORCE=1` on known events before declaring the metric trusted.\n\n2. **Corpus window mismatch**: 60 next events may span a heavily-IMPL session (high tool counts, mostly ok) or a heavily-PLAN session (lower tool counts, more decision points). Distribution variance vs prior corpus could swamp the instrumentation signal. Mitigation: log session_type per event in next telemetry pass; segment corpus by type at L-1 time.\n\n3. **Premature optimization**: focusing on metric authoring before second L-1 baseline run could lead to over-fitting to S11's specific blind spots. Mitigation: don't promote the metric function to charter (Track 7) until ≥3 corpus runs confirm the rate trends in interpretable directions.\n\n4. **Frontier-model substitution risk on classifier**: by S13, sonnet-4.6 may be replaced by sonnet-5; classifier output distribution may shift even on the same corpus. Mitigation: lock classifier model + effort in `categories-<TS>.md` frontmatter (S11 already does this — `classifier_model: sonnet`, `classifier_effort: medium`). Compare runs at same model version; flag cross-version comparisons explicitly.\n\n## What the next experiment is NOT\n\n- NOT a thesis on stocks. Pure harness-engineering loop.\n- NOT a request to ship a new skill or hook this session — the framing IS the artifact; the wiring + metric function is S13's work (per current-execution.md sequence).\n- NOT a claim that DSPy itself will be adopted. Only its metric-function pattern is borrowed.\n- NOT optimization of any frontend / runtime path. Background analysis loop only.\n\n## Provenance\n\n| Source | Path | as-of |\n|---|---|---|\n| S11 L-1 first classification | agent-workspace/learning-data/index/categories-20260429T123210Z.md | 2026-04-29 |\n| S11 session log (caveats #1+#2 origin) | agent-workspace/memory/sessions/2026-04-29-session-11.md § L-1 dispatch | 2026-04-29 |\n| S12 DSPy dogfood insight | agent-workspace/learning-data/dogfood/dspy.md | 2026-04-29 |\n| S12 research-scanner report | agent-workspace/learning-data/dogfood/agent-pick-1-research-report-20260429T131201Z.md | 2026-04-29 |\n| D-005 § 5.5d.3 | agent-workspace/memory/decisions/005-up08-track-5.5d-self-learning-pipeline.md | 2026-04-29 |\n| Charter principles 1, 3, 8, 9 | PROJECT_CHARTER.md | 2026-04-29 |\n| Capability-map L-1 (no LLM math) + L-2 (calibration metadata) | agent-workspace/memory/capability-map.md | 2026-04-29 |\n\n## Outcome (filled at next loop iteration)\n\n- next_dispatch_target: S13 (Track 5.5c.3+4+5 try-n-approaches + OTEL + JSONL extension; metric-function authoring fits naturally here)\n- expected_corpus_at_next_l1: 100-150 events (cumulative through S13 close)\n- decision_at_outcome_review: deepen confirmed | broaden | abandon — to be filled when next L-1 runs\n\n---\n\n*Generated S12 closing. {"parentUuid":"42395ddc-f08c-4b4b-96c7-292c01d84745","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01W2edCwignxBccCxzEwnwbZ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01UUbSyFs8FpKrEhCVKFmpY7","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\memory\\agent-notes.md","old_string":"### 2026-04-29 (S13-pre drift audit): Sessions MUST Update `project.md` at End-of-Session Per CLAUDE.md Protocol","new_string":"### 2026-04-29 (S13 / Track 5.5c.3 wire-in): Producer-Consumer Log Path Mismatch Silently Nulled Telemetry Field\n**Context**: `scripts/hooks/component-telemetry.sh` `correlate_failure_mode()` was reading `$MEMORY_DIR/.autonomous-stop-watchdog.log` since S8 ship. NO hook ever wrote that path. Real signals lived at `.session-hooks.log` (CLIFF + drift entries) and `.autonomous-premature-windown-alert.log` (mode-C alerts). Result: all 60 events at S11 L-1 had `failure_mode: null`. Misclassified as \"harness too clean to instrument\" in S11 caveat #2; actually was producer-consumer disconnect. Discovered S13 by tracing watchdog writers (`grep -r '.autonomous-stop-watchdog.log' scripts/` → 0 producers; `grep -r '.session-hooks.log' scripts/` → multiple producers).\n**Rule**: When a hook claims to \"correlate\" between two logs (one writing, one reading), smoke-test the producer-consumer path: (a) `grep -r '<log-path>'` returns ≥1 producer AND ≥1 consumer; (b) feed a synthetic event through the consumer and verify the field populates. If either gate fails → wire-in is vacuous; the field will silently stay at default forever. Pairs with L-S10-1 (silent ERR-trap brick) — both are \"schema appears wired but path/control flow doesn't actually populate\" failure shapes.\n**Anti-example**: Author `correlate_failure_mode()` reading `WATCHDOG_LOG=\"$MEMORY_DIR/.autonomous-stop-watchdog.log\"` without verifying any sibling hook writes that path. Six months later, classifier reads 60 events of null and concludes harness is failure-free.\n**Correct example**: S13 fix — point reader at logs with verified producers (`HOOKS_LOG=\"$MEMORY_DIR/.session-hooks.log\"` written by 4+ hooks; `MODE_C_LOG=\"$MEMORY_DIR/.autonomous-premature-windown-alert.log\"` written by `budget-watchdog.sh`) AND smoke-test 3 cases (error → \"B\", deny → \"H\", ok → null) before declaring wire-in complete.\n**Severity**: high (same severity class as L-S10-1; bricked instrumentation undetected for 4 sessions; first measurable Karpathy loop iteration was structurally impossible until fix).\n**Auto-detect**: yes — extension to `bash-hook-lint.sh` (S15 candidate): scan `scripts/hooks/*.sh` for `LOG_VAR=\"...\"` assignments where the path doesn't match any `>>` or `> \"$LOG_VAR\"` redirect in the same scripts directory. Promote to constitutional rule at Track 7 paired with L-S11-1 portability.\n\n### 2026-04-29 (S13 / Track 5.5c.3): Cumulative-vs-Windowed Metric Distinction Matters at Wire-In Boundary\n**Context**: S13 metric script `metric-failure-mode-rate.sh` defaults to CUMULATIVE rate over all events ever (321 at S13 mid-session; 2 with failure_mode → 0.62%). S12 Karpathy framing target was WINDOWED — `count(events.failure_mode != null) / count(events)` over \"next 60-event corpus\". The two interpretations differ: cumulative dilutes as denominator grows; windowed reflects current state. Pre-wire-in events (60 from S11) all have null because the field literally wasn't being populated; post-wire-in events will populate. Cumulative = 2/321 = 0.62% (well below 8.3% target); windowed last-60 = 2/60 ≈ 3.3% if just smoke tests, or higher with natural fires. Both are valid; report BOTH.\n**Rule**: For instrumentation-wire-in metrics, the metric script MUST support BOTH cumulative AND windowed measurement (`--window N` flag). At wire-in boundary, the cumulative rate misleads (drowning by pre-wire-in null-event mass) and the windowed rate is the load-bearing comparable. Default behavior for S13 = cumulative (inclusive); follow-up addition = `--window N` for windowed last-N. Document this in script header so future agents don't conflate.\n**Anti-example**: Report only cumulative (0.62%) and conclude DEEPEN failed because rate < 8.3%. Misses that the wire-in JUST happened mid-session; pre-wire-in events bias the cumulative.\n**Correct example**: Run metric in both modes; report `cumulative=2/321=0.62% / windowed-last-60=X/60=Y%` so the comparison vs S11 baseline (0/60=0%) is apples-to-apples. Document in session log + carry-over flag for next L-1 dispatch.\n**Severity**: medium (interpretation drift, not implementation bug).\n**Auto-detect**: partial — drift-detector can scan metric script invocations in session logs for missing `--window` flag when comparing to a prior baseline that was windowed. Promote to skill best-practice at Track 6 REWRITE (S14).\n\n### 2026-04-29 (S13-pre drift audit): Sessions MUST Update `project.md` at End-of-Session Per CLAUDE.md Protocol"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1181,"cache_read_input_tokens":205663,"output_tokens":2884,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1181,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":2884,"cache_read_input_tokens":205663,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1181,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1181},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYB65amfw3Y3c1F7vp6e","type":"assistant","uuid":"b2264cd9-e4bd-4c28-9a5d-e5555fa884f0","timestamp":"2026-04-29T13:53:57.230Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"09d3d5a4-dfd0-4201-ab96-9e5ba7609718","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

tokens_real=0+duration_ms=0 fingerprint discriminates synthetic from natural)\n- decision_at_outcome_review: **DEEPEN-confirmed-structurally** (wire-in works; failure_mode populates from null when conditions met). **MEASUREMENT-deferred** (target ≥8.3% awaits natural failure accumulation; Per S12 framing § Risks point #1 the discriminator works, so the metric is uncontaminated for natural-failure measurement when natural failures accumulate.\n- next_loop_iteration: S14 close re-measure with --window N=60 over post-wire-in natural events ONLY (filter `tokens_real != 0` to exclude smokes); compare to baseline 0/60.","originalFile":"---\nexperiment_id: loop-frame-20260429T131608Z\ncreated_at: 2026-04-29T13:16:08Z\nsession: S12 (Track 5.5d.3)\nframing_decision: DEEPEN\ninputs:\n  - agent-workspace/learning-data/index/categories-20260429T123210Z.md  # S11 L-1 first classification (60 events; 0/0/0/49/11 distribution)\n  - agent-workspace/learning-data/dogfood/dspy.md                       # S12 DSPy pattern insight (metric-function gap)\n  - agent-workspace/learning-data/dogfood/agent-pick-1-research-report-20260429T131201Z.md  # S12 research-scanner survey\nas_of: 2026-04-29\nmetric_function: scripts/hooks/metric-failure-mode-rate.sh  # authored S13 (Track 5.5c.3 wire-in); first-pass result documented in agent-workspace/learning-data/index/metrics-<TS>.json\n---\n\n# Karpathy Outer-Loop Frame — Experiment #1\n\n> First Karpathy autoresearch framing for stockforge harness self-learning. Per D-005 § 5.5d.3\n> Phase 7 + UP-08 verbatim \"kết hợp với idea của karpathy autoresearch\". Pattern from\n> `.claude/skills/decompose-work/SKILL.md` (try-n-approaches not yet shipped — S13).\n\n## Question\n\nGiven the corpus state at S12 close (60 events / all-ok / no failure_mode populated / 5 promotion-candidate components) and the DSPy dogfood insight (deterministic metric function is the missing bridge), what is the next experiment that maximizes information gain per token spent?\n\n## Prior state — what S11 + S12 produced\n\n**S11 (Track 5.5d.2)**: First L-1 classification dispatch. 60 events. Distribution `0/0/0/49/11` (drift / retry / mistake-type / promotion-candidate / uncategorized). Six adversarial caveats documented; two are load-bearing for this framing:\n\n- Caveat #1: drift bucket may be structurally undercount — `component-telemetry.sh` may not emit on denied tool calls.\n- Caveat #2: `failure_mode` field is null on 60/60 events — possibly uninstrumented, not falsified.\n\n**S12 (Track 5.5d.3)**: Agent-pick-1 dogfood. DSPy picked. Pattern insight: stockforge has a self-learning loop with no metric function — without a deterministic scalar/categorical comparing run N+1 to run N, no version of the pipeline can be claimed \"better than\" another.\n\n## Three options on the table\n\n### Option A — DEEPEN (instrument the missing rungs)\n\n**Action**: Wire `failure_mode` field population in `component-telemetry.sh` from `correlate_failure_mode()` already drafted in `.autonomous-stop-watchdog.log` reads. Then author **one** deterministic metric function (the `failure_mode population rate` from dogfood/dspy.md § metric candidates) and re-run L-1 on a fresh ≥60-event corpus to compare.\n\n**What it costs**: ~1 hook-edit session (~30-50K). One metric script (~30 LOC bash or python). One re-dispatch of L-1 classifier (~36K, observed cost from S11). Estimated total: 1 session ≤100K. Fits S13/S14 alongside try-n-approaches ship.\n\n**Why this option**: Two highest-confidence caveats from S11 (drift undercount + failure_mode null) both resolve via the same fix path. The DSPy dogfood ALSO points to the same gap (metric function). Three independent signals (S11 caveat #1, caveat #2, DSPy insight) converging on one fix = strong deepen prior.\n\n**What we measure** (explicit, falsifiable):\n- Metric: `failure_mode_populated = count(events where failure_mode != null) / count(events total)`\n- Baseline (S11): 0/60 = 0.0%\n- Target (S12+1): ≥ 5/60 = 8.3% on next 60-event corpus\n- Falsification: if after instrumentation, the rate is still 0% AND no failures occurred = harness too stable to instrument; loop signal exhausted; PIVOT to Option B (broaden corpus to find rare events). If rate ≥ 8.3% = instrumentation works; advance to second metric (drift signal precision).\n\n### Option B — BROADEN (grow the corpus)\n\n**Action**: Increase corpus from 60 events to 200+ before next L-1 dispatch. Currently events accumulate naturally per session (~30-60 events per major session per S11 observation). Wait 3-4 sessions and re-run L-1.\n\n**What it costs**: 0 token cost in new sessions (events emit free); 1 re-dispatch (~36K).\n\n**Why this option might be tempting**: bigger corpus = more statistical power for rare-event detection (the <5% pattern blind-spot from S11 caveat #5).\n\n**Why this option is wrong now**: at 0% failure_mode population, broadening to 200 events still yields 0/200 — adding null data doesn't improve signal. Broaden is the right move AFTER instrumentation fix; before fix, it just delays the same problem.\n\n### Option C — ABANDON (delete the zero-signal buckets)\n\n**Action**: Delete drift / retry / mistake-type categories from L-1 spec; keep only promotion-candidate + uncategorized. Acknowledge harness is too clean to have negative signal worth tracking at Phase 0 scale.\n\n**Why this option might be tempting**: simpler classifier; no instrumentation work needed.\n\n**Why this option is wrong**: it confuses \"field uninstrumented\" with \"signal absent\". S11 caveat #2 explicitly noted: \"`mistake-type` and `drift` buckets are not falsified — they are simply uninstrumented.\" Abandoning a bucket because the field hasn't been wired = closing the loop on negative information that may exist. Charter principle 3 (adversarial by design) prefers asking \"is the absence real\" over \"assume absence is real\".\n\n## Picked direction — DEEPEN (Option A)\n\nRationale: convergence of 3 independent signals on the same fix; Option B requires Option A first; Option C confuses uninstrumented with absent (charter P3 violation).\n\nCheap-first ordering doctrine satisfied: A is the smallest unit of work that resolves the most caveats per token spent.\n\n## Measurement plan (explicit; this is the metric function S13 will codify)\n\n```\nmetric: failure_mode_populated_rate\nformula: count(events where failure_mode IS NOT null) / count(events total)\nimplementation: bash + python3 oneliner in scripts/hooks/learning-index-rebuild.sh\n                (extend existing hook; do NOT add new infra)\nbaseline:    0.0% (S11 corpus, n=60, observed 2026-04-29)\ntarget:      >= 8.3% (S12+1 corpus, n>=60, observed at first L-1 re-dispatch)\nfalsification: if rate < 8.3% AND no failures occurred in the corpus window\n               (deterministically: count(.autonomous-stop-watchdog.log entries) > 0\n                vs count(events with failure_mode != null) — if log shows failures\n                but events show null, instrumentation fix was incomplete)\ncalibration:   record n_samples + lookback_window in result; per charter P8\n```\n\nThis metric is **deterministic** (counts, no LLM judgment), **falsifiable** (specific threshold), **calibration-aware** (records sample size + lookback per L-2), and **cheap** (extends an existing hook; no new dependency). Matches DSPy's metric-function pattern as adapted in dogfood/dspy.md.\n\n## Risks (≥3 distinct, per charter P3 adversarial)\n\n1. **Failure mode classifier drift**: if `correlate_failure_mode()` is buggy (e.g., over-classifies stop-watchdog entries as failures), the rate will jump artificially. Mitigation: smoke-test the function with `LEARNING_INDEX_FORCE=1` on known events before declaring the metric trusted.\n\n2. **Corpus window mismatch**: 60 next events may span a heavily-IMPL session (high tool counts, mostly ok) or a heavily-PLAN session (lower tool counts, more decision points). Distribution variance vs prior corpus could swamp the instrumentation signal. Mitigation: log session_type per event in next telemetry pass; segment corpus by type at L-1 time.\n\n3. **Premature optimization**: focusing on metric authoring before second L-1 baseline run could lead to over-fitting to S11's specific blind spots. Mitigation: don't promote the metric function to charter (Track 7) until ≥3 corpus runs confirm the rate trends in interpretable directions.\n\n4. **Frontier-model substitution risk on classifier**: by S13, sonnet-4.6 may be replaced by sonnet-5; classifier output distribution may shift even on the same corpus. Mitigation: lock classifier model + effort in `categories-<TS>.md` frontmatter (S11 already does this — `classifier_model: sonnet`, `classifier_effort: medium`). Compare runs at same model version; flag cross-version comparisons explicitly.\n\n## What the next experiment is NOT\n\n- NOT a thesis on stocks. Pure harness-engineering loop.\n- NOT a request to ship a new skill or hook this session — the framing IS the artifact; the wiring + metric function is S13's work (per current-execution.md sequence).\n- NOT a claim that DSPy itself will be adopted. Only its metric-function pattern is borrowed.\n- NOT optimization of any frontend / runtime path. Background analysis loop only.\n\n## Provenance\n\n| Source | Path | as-of |\n|---|---|---|\n| S11 L-1 first classification | agent-workspace/learning-data/index/categories-20260429T123210Z.md | 2026-04-29 |\n| S11 session log (caveats #1+#2 origin) | agent-workspace/memory/sessions/2026-04-29-session-11.md § L-1 dispatch | 2026-04-29 |\n| S12 DSPy dogfood insight | agent-workspace/learning-data/dogfood/dspy.md | 2026-04-29 |\n| S12 research-scanner report | agent-workspace/learning-data/dogfood/agent-pick-1-research-report-20260429T131201Z.md | 2026-04-29 |\n| D-005 § 5.5d.3 | agent-workspace/memory/decisions/005-up08-track-5.5d-self-learning-pipeline.md | 2026-04-29 |\n| Charter principles 1, 3, 8, 9 | PROJECT_CHARTER.md | 2026-04-29 |\n| Capability-map L-1 (no LLM math) + L-2 (calibration metadata) | agent-workspace/memory/capability-map.md | 2026-04-29 |\n\n## Outcome (filled at next loop iteration)\n\n- next_dispatch_target: S13 (Track 5.5c.3+4+5 try-n-approaches + OTEL + JSONL extension; metric-function authoring fits naturally here)\n- expected_corpus_at_next_l1: 100-150 events (cumulative through S13 close)\n- decision_at_outcome_review: deepen confirmed | broaden | abandon — to be filled when next L-1 runs\n\n---\n\n*Generated S12 closing.
